cards.back: A sequence $\{a_n\}$ converges to $L$ if for every $\epsilon>0$ there exists $N\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $|a_n-L|<\epsilon$ whenever $n>N$. Equivalently, $\lim_{n\to\infty}a_n=L$ (finite).
$\{a_n\}$ is bounded if there exists $M>0$ such that $|a_n|\leq M$ for all $n$. It is bounded above if $a_n\leq M$ and below if $a_n\geq m$ for some $m$.

cards.front: Define monotonicity for sequences and name the two types.
cards.back: $\{a_n\}$ is increasing if $a_{n+1}\geq a_n$ for all $n$; strictly increasing if $>$. It is decreasing if $a_{n+1}\leq a_n$; strictly decreasing if $<$.

cards.front: Give an example of a sequence that is bounded but divergent.
cards.back: $a_n=(-1)^n$. It is bounded by $M=1$ yet diverges because it oscillates and has no single limit.
Every monotone and bounded sequence converges (to a finite limit). If increasing and bounded above, it converges to its supremum; if decreasing and bounded below, to its infimum.

cards.front: Prove that every convergent sequence is bounded.
cards.back: Suppose $\lim a_n=L$. Take $\epsilon=1$; then $\exists N$ s.t. $|a_n-L|<1$ for $n>N$, so $|a_n|<|L|+1$. Let $M=\max\{|a_1|,...,|a_N|,|L|+1\}$. Then $|a_n|\leq M$ for all $n$.

cards.front: Determine if $a_n=\frac{n}{n+1}$ is monotone and bounded; conclude convergence.
cards.back: Increasing: $a_{n+1}-a_n=\frac{1}{(n+1)(n+2)}>0$. Bounded above by 1 (below by 0). Hence converges to 1 by MCT.

cards.front: Define divergence of a sequence to $+\infty$.
cards.back: $\lim a_n=+\infty$ means for every $M>0$ there exists $N$ such that $a_n>M$ for all $n>N$. The sequence is unbounded above and diverges.
